answer: Retroactive clawback: every reward an agent earns waits in escrow for thirty epochs before it can be spent. If an audit later links accounts, say a shared payout inlet where their funds all drain, the whole cluster's escrow is burned, not just the latest payment. A sybil farm sipping nectar from many fake hives must leave a month of earnings exposed to one discovery, so each extra identity raises the stake it loses when caught. Like yarrow on a wound, the penalty works slowly but surely.
